name: KitchenCupboard
description: Kitchen Cupboard is a self-hosted recipe library, weekly meal planner and collaborative shopping list for households. Share recipes, ratings, a regular-purchase Basics checklist and pantry flags; plan batch cooking and leftovers, then review combined ingredients before adding them to shopping. Includes real-time list updates, recipe website imports, text/PDF/CSV exports and a mobile-friendly PWA with offline shopping-item edits. Photo extraction through a configured vision provider and one-way Nextcloud calendar sync are optional. Recipes and planning are shared across all active accounts; shopping lists have separate sharing permissions. This is a beta, and the latest image follows main. Set a random SECRET_KEY before starting, then create the first admin account locally; later registrations require invitations by default. HTTPS is needed for browser PWA/offline support except on localhost.

paths.name: Data Path
paths.description: Persistent SQLite database, recipe uploads and integration encryption key. Back up the entire directory before updating. The app runs as UID/GID 1001 after the entrypoint adjusts permissions.

variables.name: Secret Key
variables.description: REQUIRED: Enter a random JWT signing key of at least 32 characters. Generate with: python3 -c 'import secrets; print(secrets.token_urlsafe(64))'. Keep it stable across updates. The app refuses to start with a missing or short key.

variables.name: Registration Enabled
variables.description: Leave false to require invitations after initial setup. The first registered user becomes admin without an invite, even when this is false; create that account before public exposure. Set true only for open registration.

variables.name: Public URL
variables.description: Set to the full URL users open, including http:// or https:// and any non-default port. Used for recipe links in Nextcloud calendar events. Replace localhost with your server address or public hostname.

variables.name: Integration LAN Hosts
variables.description: Optional comma-separated hostnames of internal HTTPS Nextcloud or vision servers. Use hostnames only, without schemes or paths. TLS certificates are still verified. Leave empty for public endpoints only.

variables.name: CORS Origins
variables.description: Optional comma-separated browser origins allowed to call the API. Leave empty for same-origin only; command-line and server-side agents do not require this.
